Subject: MAP + order-form sequencing — acceptance lanes and owners

Hi Samantha / Cardinal team,

Attached is our working MAP (Cardinal_MAP_v3.xlsx) and a near-final order form draft. I pulled together a short sequencing proposal so we can lock milestones without blocking the commercial signature:

- MSA signature (legal majority agreed) = required before production access; target week of 7/6
- DPA review (privacy) = run in parallel with MSA legal redlines; aim to finish by 7/3
- Order form (pricing + SKU) = finalize after pricing QA; can be executed immediately after MSA if legal redlines are limited

Specific asks for you:
1) Confirm that Cardinal is comfortable with MSA-first approach (MSA > Order form) or if procurement requires order-form first to start your internal PO process.
2) Share any mandatory acceptance/acceptance-testing gates you need inside the MAP spreadsheet under the acceptance tab.

If helpful, I can convert the MAP into a two-week sprint checklist with owners for each lane (legal, security, procurement, product). Laura / Karthik — flag anything I should call out for Redwood legal or security.

Attachments: Cardinal_MAP_v3.xlsx, OrderForm_Draft_20260629.docx

Thanks,
Rachel

Hi Rachel,

Thanks — quick clarifying questions from procurement: we typically need an executed order form to open an internal purchase order (PO) queue, but legal can do the MSA in parallel as long as the order form doesn't contain any commercial commitments that contradict the MSA.

Two asks from our side: 1) Can you mark any order-form fields that are "placeholder pricing" in the draft so procurement can move a PO into the system with a pending final price? 2) We require explicit acceptance-test criteria for our QA before we sign off (pass/fail checklist) — can your team fill those into the acceptance tab?

I looped in Jonah for legal redlines. Once Jonah gives a sense of the redline scope we can tell procurement if we can open a PO pending final price.

Samantha

From: Jonah Park <j.park@cardinalbio.com>
To: Samantha Li <s.li@cardinalbio.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP + order-form sequencing — acceptance lanes and owners

Rachel / Samantha — quick note from legal after a preliminary pass. Attaching our redline bundle (Cardinal_Redlines_OrderForm.docx) for your review. High-level comments:

- We have three priority edits that affect sequencing: 1) a clause tying acceptance to a short-term pilot (explicit pass/fail criteria), 2) a limitation-of-liability tweak for data processing during the pilot, and 3) indemnity language that we want to keep scoped to third-party data breaches only.
- If Redwood accepts the pilot-acceptance gating language, we can proceed with procurement opening a PO referencing "pilot quantities" and allow the order-form to be executed concurrently with the MSA being finalized.
- If Redwood cannot accept the gating language, procurement insists on an executed order form before PO entry.

I'll keep the redlines targeted — looking to avoid prolonged back-and-forth. Laura / Karthik: if you want, I can run the redlines by your counsel to speed alignment.

Attachments: Cardinal_Redlines_OrderForm.docx

Jonah Park
Counsel — Cardinal Bio
[j.park@cardinalbio.com]

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Li <s.li@cardinalbio.com>, Jonah Park <j.park@cardinalbio.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP + order-form sequencing — acceptance lanes and owners

Thanks Jonah — and thanks Samantha.

We reviewed the redlines with Redwood legal and product. Summary and proposed sequencing that should satisfy procurement without delaying the commercial timeline:

1) Acceptance gating: we can accept a short-term pilot with explicit pass/fail criteria inside the MAP acceptance tab. Redwood will commit to the pilot acceptance window (14 days) and clear pass/fail metrics. If pilot passes, the order form converts to full subscription automatically.

2) Limitation of liability and indemnity: Redwood legal accepts scoped indemnity limited to third-party data breaches and will propose tightened language to Jonah today.

3) Parallel execute path (recommended):
   - Step A (now): Cardinal opens a provisional PO referencing "pilot quantities" against the draft order form (procurement indicated they can do this if pilot gating is explicit).
   - Step B (ASAP): Redwood and Cardinal execute the MSA (signature by 7/6 target).
   - Step C (in-parallel): DPA review and security evidence exchange (Redwood to deliver Redteam report + Redwood_Security_Clauses_v2.pdf link) completed by 7/3; any security items that block production will be listed in the MAP with owners and SLAs.
   - Step D (post-pilot): If pilot passes, Cardinal converts the provisional PO to production order and we finalize order-form pricing.

Next steps / owners:
- Samantha / Procurement: open provisional PO referencing "pilot quantities" and confirm internal PO ID. (Samantha)
- Jonah: confirm if the indemnity tweaks below are acceptable; Rachel will ingest small edits and return a clean MSA redline. (Jonah)
- Laura: coordinate with Redwood product on pass/fail metric wording; add to MAP acceptance tab by EOD tomorrow. (Laura)
- Karthik / Priyom: stand by for security evidence upload and enclave controls doc to be shared to the Drive link. (Karthik, Priyom)

I've attached an updated order-form that highlights placeholder pricing so procurement can move the PO. Attachment: OrderForm_Draft_20260629.docx. Also linking HubSpot: HubSpot-Deal-CRD-2026-1784 for record-keeping.

If we get sign-off on the high-level approach today, we can keep the current go-live target of mid-July.

Thanks all — short replies welcome (thumbs-up or explicit "OK to open PO").

Best,
Rachel
Senior Sales Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
